paper_metadata.title: Neuroimaging of sport concussion: persistent alterations in brain structure and function at medical clearance

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study clearly defines the source population (varsity athletes) and uses a matched control design. Inclusion criteria and recruitment settings are well-described. While it is a single-center study, the characteristics of the sample are transparently reported.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Fifty-four (54) athletes were recruited from interuniversity ("varsity") teams at a single institution.
items.reasoning: The target population is clearly identified as varsity athletes from a specific institutional setting.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Twenty-seven (27) athletes were recruited following a physician diagnosis of concussion... Formal physician evaluation for suspected concussion was aligned with the standardized framework set forth by the Concussion in Sport Group
items.reasoning: Recruitment followed a standardized clinical framework (CISG) and physician diagnosis, reducing selection bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The attrition rate is very low (2 out of 27 concussed athletes), and the reasons for exclusion from specific analyses are transparently reported. The high completion rate (89% for longitudinal analysis) limits the risk of attrition bias.

items.evidence_snippet: Two athletes with concussion were not imaged at RTP due to drop-out, while one athlete was scanned at RTP but did not have acute imaging, leaving 24 athletes with complete acute and RTP scans.
items.reasoning: 24/27 (89%) of the concussed cohort completed the longitudinal protocol, which is well above the 80% threshold.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (concussion) is defined by clinical diagnosis and the measurement tools (3T MRI) are objective, standardized, and described in high technical detail. The use of automated pipelines (FSL, AFNI) reduces subjective measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Twenty-seven (27) athletes were recruited following a physician diagnosis of concussion... Formal physician evaluation for suspected concussion was aligned with the standardized framework set forth by the Concussion in Sport Group

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were imaged at St. Michael's Hospital, using an MRI system operating at 3 Tesla (Magnetom Skyra, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)... DTI and fMRI sequences were acquired
items.reasoning: Advanced neuroimaging (3T MRI) is an objective and reliable method for measuring the biological state of the brain.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Diffusion tensor imaging was used to measure fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD)... resting-state functional MRI was used to measure global functional connectivity (Gconn).
items.reasoning: The study uses continuous neuroimaging metrics (FA, MD, Gconn) rather than arbitrary categorical cut-points.

items.reasoning: Standardized equipment and location were used for all subjects.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (medical clearance/RTP) is defined by a multi-modal clinical protocol. While RTP is a clinical decision, the study uses it as a time-point to measure objective brain changes, and the criteria for that time-point are clearly specified.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Medical clearance to RTP was determined by normal Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3) scores, along with successful completion of both a graded exercise protocol consistent with consensus guidelines and a computerized cognitive screening battery.
items.reasoning: The outcome (RTP) is defined by a rigorous, multi-component clinical protocol.

items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Medical clearance to RTP was determined by normal Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3) scores... and a computerized cognitive screening battery.
items.reasoning: The use of standardized tools (SCAT3, cognitive battery) increases the reliability of the clinical outcome measurement.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study matches controls for age, sex, and concussion history, which is a strength. However, it does not explicitly adjust for other potential confounders like medication use, sub-concussive impacts during the recovery period, or specific sport type in the multivariable models.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses sophisticated multivariate techniques (PLS) and non-parametric bootstrapping, which are appropriate for neuroimaging data with small samples. The reporting is transparent, including both significant and non-significant findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariate Partial Least Squares (PLS) analysis was performed for each of the MRI measures (FA, MD, Gconn)... Repeated-measures bootstrap resampling was used to generate empirical distributions
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline is described in detail, including software and statistical parameters.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The first PLS component is reported for each of the analyzed MRI measures, which explains the greatest total covariance across groups.
items.reasoning: The use of PLS to identify multivariate patterns is a standard and appropriate framework for this type of exploratory neuroimaging study.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Repeated-measures bootstrap resampling was used... resampling units consisting of a subject's acute and RTP scans, along with their matched control.
items.reasoning: The model correctly accounts for the longitudinal, matched-pair nature of the data.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Neither of the DTI measures showed significant association between brain changes at RTP... However, changes in Gconn were significantly related to time to RTP
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant (Gconn) and non-significant (DTI) associations with recovery time, suggesting no selective reporting bias.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Statistical Analysis and Presentation Summary
